personal.residency_info_toggle: Want a better refund? Read this before choosing
personal.residency_info_title: 💡 Your residency status can significantly affect your refund
personal.residency_info_intro: The ATO uses 4 tests to determine if you are an Australian tax resident. If you meet any of them, you may be entitled to a much larger refund — because residents pay a lower tax rate and can access the tax-free threshold (first $18,200 tax-free). We recommend calling the ATO to confirm your status.
personal.residency_test1_desc: Do you live in Australia in the ordinary sense? The ATO weighs physical presence, intention, family and work ties, assets, and social life. No single factor is decisive.
personal.residency_test2_desc: Is your legal domicile in Australia? Applies unless you have a permanent place of abode established overseas.
personal.residency_test3_desc: Were you in Australia for 183 days or more during the tax year? If you arrived during the year, this test may apply to you.
personal.residency_test4_desc: Applies to Australian government employees posted overseas (diplomats, etc.) and their families.
personal.residency_info_cta: If you think you may meet any of these tests, call the ATO before lodging your return. It can make a significant difference to your refund.
personal.first_time_hint: This information helps us prepare your return correctly.
personal.first_time_question: Is this the first time you're claiming a tax return in Australia?
personal.first_time_info: If you have never filed a tax return in Australia, select Yes. This helps us determine which financial years you can claim.

personal.occupation_placeholder: E.g: Hospitality worker, Construction labourer, Farm hand...
personal.occupation_hint: Enter the main occupation for which you received salary or wages during the financial year.
personal.occupation_tip: Your occupation determines what deductions you can claim. For example: if you're a photographer or video editor working with ABN, you can deduct cameras, lenses or editing equipment. Be specific about what you actually did to maximise your refund.
personal.australian_resident_info: Your tax residency status affects the rate the ATO applies. Working Holiday Makers (visa 417/462) are taxed at a flat 15%. Australian residents have an $18,200 tax-free threshold.
personal.tax_residency_hint: Your tax residency status determines the tax rate applied by the ATO.
personal.bank_hint: The ATO transfers the refund directly to this account. Make sure the details are correct.
personal.abn_warning: Did you work with an ABN? If at any point during the financial year you worked as an independent contractor, you must declare that income. Fill in this field and upload proof in Documentation → ABN income.

of RETAUX. By proceeding, I understand and agree to the following:

About the service: RETAUX is a platform that connects clients with registered tax agents. RETAUX does not lodge returns directly with the ATO — your tax return is prepared and lodged by a registered tax agent (ENPRESA of Accounting & Finance) on your behalf.

Referral arrangement disclosure: RETAUX receives a financial benefit from the registered tax agent for organising and referring clients. This benefit is included in the price you pay to RETAUX and does not represent an additional cost to you. If you used another user's referral code, that person also receives a AUD 20 credit for referring you.

Billing & deductibility: Because RETAUX acts as a service intermediary, only the registered tax agent's fee — not the full amount paid to RETAUX — is deductible as a tax agent cost (D10) in your next year's tax return. The actual refund you would receive from that deduction is a fraction of that fee, based on your marginal tax rate (typically a few dollars). The impact on you is minimal.

Processing time: Once your documents are complete and your return is lodged, the ATO typically takes 30 to 45 days to process and issue your refund. RETAUX aims to lodge within 2 weeks of receiving all your documents, but we cannot control ATO processing times or those of the registered tax agent.

linking.subtitle: To manage your return we need you to authorise us as your agent with the ATO. This is done using a linking code that you generate yourself in your ATO online services account — never with your myGov password.

linking.how_title: How to generate your code (on your phone or computer)
linking.step1: Go to myGov and open ATO online services.
linking.step2: Go to Profile → Authorised contacts and agents (or "Agent details").
linking.step3: Look for "Add new linking code" or "Generate linking code" and generate a code. You'll see an alphanumeric code.
linking.step4: Important: this code expires after 7 days. Copy and paste it below as soon as you generate it — so your agent can use it in time.
linking.step5: Paste the code in the form and submit. That's it — no further action needed on your end.
linking.code_hint: We will only use this to link as your agent. It is not your myGov password.
linking.why_title: Why this step and not your myGov password?
linking.why_body: Because myGov prohibits sharing your password with third parties, and because the linking code is the official ATO mechanism for authorising a registered agent — it's safer for you and it's the correct procedure.

deductions.title: Tax deductions
deductions.subtitle: These deductions reduce your taxable income and increase your refund.
deductions.d1_info: You can claim kilometres travelled between different jobs, client visits, or carrying heavy tools. The cents per kilometre method (88c/km) applies with a maximum of 5,000 km. No receipts needed — just a reasonable estimate.
deductions.d2_info: You can claim flights, trains, taxis, Uber and accommodation paid for work trips to a different location than your usual workplace. Does NOT include your daily home-to-work commute. Receipt required for each expense.
deductions.d3_info: Includes compulsory uniforms with employer logo, protective clothing (safety boots, helmets, gloves) and laundry costs for that clothing. Conventional clothing cannot be claimed even if worn only for work. No receipts needed for laundry up to $150.
deductions.d4_info:
You can claim courses, books or study materials directly related to your current job (not a future one). Receipt required if the total exceeds $300 in work-related expenses.

* Upload the payment receipt (invoice or bank statement), not the course certificate.
deductions.d5_title: D5 — Other work-related expenses (technology, certifications, etc.)
deductions.d5_info: Includes: work licences and certifications (RSA, White Card, etc.), work use of phone and internet (% of use), tools and equipment under $300, professional subscriptions and memberships. No receipts needed if total work expenses are $300 or less.
deductions.d9_info: You can claim donations to Australian DGR (Deductible Gift Recipient) registered organisations. Receipt required for amounts over $2. Raffles, lotteries and memberships cannot be claimed.
deductions.d6_title: D6 — Home office / Working from home
deductions.d6_info: Enter the total home office expenses for the financial year. The ATO allows the fixed rate method (AUD 0.67 per hour worked from home, no individual receipts needed) or the actual cost method (proportional electricity, internet and rent, with invoices). Upload your bills in the documents section above.
deductions.d10_info: You can claim the amount paid to a tax agent or accountant in the previous year to prepare your tax return. This year's RETAUX service is also deductible next year. Receipt required.
deductions.car_purchase_hint: Purchase price or market value at the time of work use
deductions.d1_receipt_note: No receipt needed for the cents-per-km method (up to 5,000 km). A receipt is only required if you use the actual depreciation method and kilometres exceed 5,000.
deductions.d10_auto_note: The cost of our service (RETAUX) is automatically deductible in your next tax return. No action needed — we calculate it for you.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.subtitle: Last updated: July 2025 · RETAUX · hola@retaux.com
privacy.s1_body: RETAUX is an Australian tax return preparation service for temporary visa holders. We operate in Australia and primarily serve Spanish-speaking clients. You can contact us at hola@retaux.com.
privacy.s2_intro: To provide the service we need the following personal data:
privacy.s2_li1: Full name, date of birth and nationality
privacy.s2_li2: Australian address and contact details (email, phone)
privacy.s2_li3: Tax File Number (TFN) and Australian Business Number (ABN, if applicable)
privacy.s2_li5: Bank details for tax refund (BSB and account number)
privacy.s2_li6: Employment documents: payslips, payment summaries, certificates
privacy.s3_li1: Prepare and lodge your tax return with the ATO
privacy.s3_li2: Schedule your appointment and communicate with you
privacy.s3_li4: Send you confirmations, updates and reminders
privacy.s3_note: We do not use your data for advertising and never sell it to third parties.
privacy.s4_title: 4. Who we share your data with
privacy.s4_intro: We only share information with providers strictly necessary to operate:
privacy.s4_li1: ATO (Australian Taxation Office) — to lodge your return
privacy.s4_li2: Stripe — payment processing (we do not store card data)
privacy.s4_note: All these providers have their own privacy policies and comply with international security standards.
privacy.s5_li1: The site operates exclusively over HTTPS (encrypted connection)
privacy.s5_li2: Access credentials are stored encrypted with bcrypt — never in plain text
privacy.s5_li3: Access to the admin panel is restricted to authorised staff
privacy.s5_li4: We implement active protection against bots and automated registrations
privacy.s5_li5: We perform daily database backups to secure external storage
privacy.s5_li6: Documents you upload are stored on a private server with restricted access
privacy.s6_title: 6. How long we keep your data
privacy.s6_body: We keep your information while the service is active and for the period required by Australian tax law (generally 5 years). Once that period expires, we delete or anonymise the data.
privacy.s7_li1: Access the data we hold about you
privacy.s7_li3: Request deletion of your data (right to be forgotten)
privacy.s7_li4: Withdraw your consent at any time
privacy.s7_note: To exercise any of these rights, email us at hola@retaux.com and we will respond within 48 hours.
privacy.s8_body: We use a single session cookie (retaux_token) to keep you logged in while using the site. We do not use tracking or advertising cookies.
privacy.s9_body: We may update this policy when necessary. In case of significant changes we will notify you by email. The current version is always available on this page.
privacy.contact_note: Questions about this policy? Email us at hola@retaux.com — we respond within 48 hours.

doc_cat.payslips_desc: Pay slips from each job. If you don't have them all, upload at least the last one per employer for the financial year.
doc_cat.abn_income_desc: If you worked as a freelancer or contractor with an ABN: invoices, payment receipts or any record with dates and amounts received during the financial year.
doc_cat.logbook_desc: Logbook of work km, fuel receipts, servicing costs or toll receipts. Required if you use your car for work (between jobs, client visits, carrying heavy tools). Does NOT include daily home-to-work travel.
doc_cat.work_travel_desc: Flights, trains, ferries, taxis, Uber receipts or accommodation paid to travel to a different work site. Does NOT include your daily home-to-work commute.
doc_cat.certifications_desc: Proof of payment for licences required for your job (RSA, White Card, etc.) or union/professional association fees.
doc_cat.training_desc: Proof of payment for courses, workshops or study materials directly related to your current job. Upload the payment receipt, not the course certificate.
doc_cat.work_expenses_desc: Receipts for uniforms with employer logo, protective clothing (safety boots, helmets, gloves) or laundry costs for those items. Conventional clothing is not deductible even if worn only for work.
doc_cat.tech_purchases_label: D5 — Technology, phone & other work expenses
doc_cat.tech_purchases_desc: Invoices for mobile phone, data plan, computer, accessories or tools used for work. Also fuel and car servicing if applicable. Upload the payment receipt.
doc_cat.tech_purchases_tip: You can also upload invoices for mobile phone plans (work-use portion), petrol and car servicing if you use your car for work. These expenses may contribute to your refund — upload the receipt and our team will assess what applies.
doc_cat.investment_statements_desc: Investment account statement (shares, ETFs, crypto). Must show gains, losses and dividends for the financial year. Required if you have interest income, dividend income or related deductions.
doc_cat.donation_receipts_desc: Official receipts from DGR (Deductible Gift Recipient) registered organisations in Australia. Only deductible if the entity is DGR registered. Raffle tickets and lottery entries do not qualify.
doc_cat.home_office_desc: Electricity, internet or other household bills related to working remotely. Upload the full period bills — our team will calculate the deductible percentage.
doc_cat.home_office_info: You can claim a portion of your household expenses if you worked from home. This includes electricity and internet bills (based on the percentage used for work), and optionally rent or mortgage if you have a dedicated workspace. The ATO accepts the fixed rate method (AUD 0.67/hour worked from home) or the actual cost method with receipts. Upload the relevant bills for the financial year.

calc.where_to_find: 📄 You can find these values in your Payment Summary or in myGov → ATO → Employment. If you don't have access to myGov, ask your employer directly.
calc.income_info: Your total income earned in Australia. Find it in your Income Statement on myGov → ATO → Employment.
calc.payg_info: The tax your employer deducted from your wages. Also on your Income Statement in myGov → ATO.
calc.deductions_info: Work-related expenses: uniforms, tools, travel to work sites, union fees. Only what you paid out of pocket.
calc.disclaimer: ⚠️ This calculator is for guidance only. RETAUX will calculate your exact refund using your official documents.
calc.penalty_title: ⏰ What happens if you don't pay on time?
calc.penalty_body: The ATO applies a General Interest Charge (GIC, approx. 11% p.a.) on unpaid amounts from the due date. Additionally, failing to lodge on time can result in a penalty of up to AUD 1,650. Filing and paying on time avoids these extra costs.

super.title: Payment — Superannuation (DASP)
super.subtitle: We handle your superannuation claim with the ATO.
super.info_banner: If you worked in Australia, your employer deposited a percentage of your salary into a superannuation fund. You can claim it back when you leave the country. Processing takes approximately 28 business days.
super.step2: Use the Revolut link to pay securely.
super.step3: Once paid, click «I've already paid» so we can confirm your payment.
